text:
Maya: Heads-up — opened a docs PR adding a "structured output quickstart" focusing on tool-returned arrays and guardrails. Need review on schema examples and SDK parse patterns.
Ibrahim: link? I'll take a look.
Maya: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5012 — highlights: 1) concise schema templates for list-of-objects, 2) migration note for parse_json vs old implicit parse, 3) small CLI snippet showing ajv validation for examples.
Lena: skimmed. Recommend adding "minItems: 1" on arrays where empty result is semantically invalid. Also suggest an explicit example of a safe fallback in JS.
Elliot: For JS fallback, propose using parseJson + validation:
```ts
const resp = await client.callTool('find_entities', input);
const parsed = parseJson(resp.text);
if (!Array.isArray(parsed) || parsed.length === 0) {
  // fallback: return a helpful message or call a different tool
}
```
Maya: good — I'll add that snippet. Also adding a note for docs CI: mark partial examples with frontmatter "example: partial" to skip ajv.
docs-bot: deploy preview queued — https://deploy-preview-5012--docs.redwood.example :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Ibrahim: tiny nit: the Python snippet should use response.parse_json() not response.json() — consistent with SDK.
Lena: +1. Also add a short troubleshooting FAQ: "Why did my array become empty?" pointing to model prompt design and minItems guardrail.
Maya: will push edits in ~20m and request reviews from @Lena and @Ibrahim. Thanks all! :sparkles:
